mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last two months indicates a strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points over the last month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between UNRATE decreases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the last two months signals increased economic activity and supply, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the last month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% year-over-year and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points over the last three months, it signals strong economic growth coupled with a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 2% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3pp in 3 months
regime_hint: economic expansion with labor market tightening
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of strong GDPC1 growth and decreasing UNRATE on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
